plain_description.what: Checks that renaming local variables in two copy-pasted blocks of a split-significance test does not change its output. The site-null CSV is produced before and after the rename and compared byte by byte (no judge calls).
plain_description.why: The two blocks were identical, so an edit could land in the wrong one and still compile. The rename removes that hazard, but only if it is truly inert.
plain_description.information: Identical outputs, plus proof that the renamed code actually ran, show the rename is safe. Any byte difference would mean the two arms were not independent. Result: done, passed. The CSVs are byte-identical, and compiled classes show the new code ran. This covers the 'site-null' arm only and fixes one instance of the hazard, not the whole class.
